_why: The authority names are checked against (NAME1, D116; docs/2026-10-01-naming-design.md). A name is part of its element, designed in each language: `terms` holds one name per concept in each language, chosen as a name rather than translated, with what it must not be called; `kinds` holds the fourteen kinds of element with their budgets and the keys of each kind, the most specific entry winning and a key no kind names a sentence; `doors` pairs each door with the key naming its destination; `accepted` keeps each budget judgement looked at and kept, with the name it accepted and why (NAME2). It sits beside the language folders and in neither, so it is never merged into a catalogue. scripts/names-check.mjs reads it and reports; NAME1b turns the facts' half to a gate.

measure._why: English is counted in characters; Chinese in units, a Chinese character or full-width mark 1 and anything else 1/2, since the system's Latin face averages half an em. A placeholder counts as its typical value.

nav.what: A place a person goes to: the activity bar (its tip and the view's header), Settings' domain list, the menu bar's seven menus and the one they fold into.
nav.room: Settings' domain list: 11rem less its padding and rail, 150px of text-body on one line; one word on the bar's tip.

title.what: The name of what is open: a view's page header, a drawer's title, a window's title.
title.room: A drawer's title: 32rem less its padding and close, about 430px of text-title.

tab.what: One of the views a region holds: the side bar's and the panel's tabs.
tab.room: The selected tab whole beside three icon tabs, the side bar at its 300px floor: about 66px of text-small.

section.what: The name of a part of a page: SectionTitle, CardHeader, a sub-head in a card, a menu's group label.
section.room: One line in a card in Settings' narrowest column, about 260px of text-small, semibold.

field.what: The name of a value or a setting: SettingRow's label, a form's label, a record's dt, a tile's label, a checkbox's label.
field.room: A settings row's label column floor, 16rem (256px) of text-body.

choice.what: One of the values offered: a segmented option, a select's option.
choice.room: A segmented option, its whole group on one line in a row: about 90px of text-small.

button.what: An act: Button, an icon-only control's name, a link that acts.
button.room: Two buttons side by side in the side bar at its floor: about 110px of text-body each.

status.what: A word for a state: Pill, a dot's word, a Chip, the status bar's nouns and values.
status.room: A pill beside its row's title: about 100px of text-meta in the pill's mono face.

menu.what: An item in a menu or the palette: the strip's menus, a tab list's menu, a row's menu, the command palette.
menu.room: A strip menu at its 224px minimum, less the check, icon and shortcut columns: about 140px of text-small.

command.what: A row of the command palette: a command's name, then a dash and its gloss, which is a sentence.
command.room: The palette's 34rem less its padding and the row's icon, about 470px of text-body; the name before the dash is measured.

headline.room: An empty state in the side bar at its floor: about 270px of text-body, semibold.

placeholder.what: The hint inside an empty field.
placeholder.room: Inside a field in a 309px row: about 250px of text-body.

toast.what: An act's outcome, said once, in one sentence.
toast.room: The 26rem toast clamped to two lines: about 720px of text-body; past it the sentence is cut.

sentence.what: The platform explaining itself, and a row's meta fragments: a hint, a tip, a body, a description, 'filed 2d ago'.

terms.means: The view that opens the day: what needs you, the tiles, what is outstanding.
One agent's run in one repository, started by the driver for a quest or by the person as a chat.
A session the person started to talk with its agent, rather than one the driver started for a quest.
terms.why: VS Code's zh-CN names its Chat view 聊天; 对话 is the conversation every structured session keeps.

terms.means: What a session and its person said, kept as typed events and shown in Sessions' centre.
A request from one repository to another, published to the service and taken by whoever owns that code.
terms.why: 任务 is the family's word for a task, which a quest is not (POLISH4).

terms.means: What a person asks of a workspace; the declarations or its intake turn it into quests.
terms.why: 请求 is every request's word (a pull request's, an HTTP request's, an agent's for more); 需求 names what a person wants made. The owner's call.

terms.means: Not a name on the window: a request to a repository is a quest, and one to a workspace an ask.
What reads an ask and decides which repositories it becomes quests for: the declarations, or a session on an agent.
What the person says holds for every session in one repository (which writes are allowed, where to test), kept on this machine and handed to each session beneath its quest (KNOWUSE1b).
terms.why: 长期 says it outlives the quest it was first said on; 答复 is the person's answer, not a rule an agent may change.

terms.means: The language a repository's or a workspace's sessions are asked to write to the person in (their questions, closing notes, decline reasons and last words), set for the work, the repository's winning; never the window's language, which is its viewer's (LANG1c, D142).
terms.why: 会话 is the glossary's session; 语言 names the language, as the window's own is 语言 in Appearance. 对话 is the conversation, and the setting governs the session's writing, not the conversation view.

terms.means: The person's yes for one act outside a repository (a production write, a release, a push, a sign-in), asked once on the ask and handed to every session on it (KNOWUSE1a).
terms.why: 放行 is to let an act through a gate that was the person's to open; 许可 reads as a licence or a permission rule, which is the agents' permissions.

terms.means: The repository a quest is addressed to.
terms.why: It pairs with the asker's 委托方, both built on 委托.

terms.means: The repository a quest comes from.
What a repository says of itself in daoris.json: what it is, what it owns and what it accepts.
The part of a declaration naming what a repository is responsible for.
The part of a declaration naming the quests a repository takes.
Quests that follow one another, each published when the one before it closes done.

How a repository's work moves from the agent's work to its last stage: which steps, in what order, who takes part in each and what is automatic (D157). Current is the one drawn from the rules as they stand; a chain is its work step.
terms.why: 工作流 is what a workflow tool's Chinese calls one. 工作流转 is How this work ran, a chain's story, and 流程 is any process at all (WORKFLOW1b).

terms.means: One piece of work following its workflow: a chain's work in one repository, read as steps from its records, so where it stands is said step by step (D157 §5.1, WORKFLOW1c).
terms.why: 运行 is a process running and 工作流转 is How this work ran, a chain's story (D157 §1); 进展 is how far a piece of work has come, which is what a run shows.

terms.means: A name a workspace gives a sort of work, such as Documentation or Feature, which chooses the workflow work of that sort follows (D157 §4.2).
terms.why: 类型 is a sort of thing; 任务 is the family's word for a task, which a quest is not.

terms.means: Hand a quest to the service, where its receiver pulls it.
A repository's agent accepts a quest to work on; the quest is then taken (已接下).
A quest's work finished, or a session finished by its person; the state is 已完成.
Turn down a quest, a parked session or a proposal, with a reason whoever reads the record can act on.
terms.why: 拒绝 is the rules' deny, and the system's refusal.

terms.means: The rules' list of what an agent must never do, beside allow (允许) and ask (询问).
End an ask, or a quest by done or declined; the state is 已关闭.
Remove a record for good: a quest, an ask.
Remove from this machine what it kept of finished work: its records, their words and the files they left; a team's remote keeps its copy. A setting cleared goes back to its default.
terms.why: Delete (删除) removes a record for good and a quest's delete travels to every machine, where a clear never travels; clean up (清理) is landed trees and branches, which a clear never touches; 清空 empties a container and says nothing of what stays (HIST1e, D153 §8).

terms.means: Take something out of a list or a setting; what it named stays where it was.
Take a repository out of the registry; nothing in it is deleted.
Add a repository to the registry, so the service knows where it is.
terms.why: The registry is 注册表, and 注册 and 登记 were fifteen strings each.

terms.means: Register every repository in a folder at once.
A git repository the family knows, owned by its own agent.
terms.why: The Projects view lists repositories, and every row, button and sentence in it says so; the owner's call.

terms.means: The repositories that share quests, knowledge and records with one another; a row per repository in the registry.
The code's old word for a workspace (D75); never on the window.
Every repository the service knows, across workspaces.
A repository's own folder on this machine, the one the registry names.
A working tree of a session's own beside the checkout, so sessions in one repository do not collide.
A git branch; a session works on one of its own.
A part of a repository it declares for work, with paths of its own, which a quest addresses as repository:lane so that lane's sessions take it.
terms.why: 泳道 is a swimlane, the word a Chinese process board gives one lane of work beside others; 车道 is a road's, and 通道 a channel's. DEV4 named it before the glossary had a term (NAME2).

terms.means: The branch a repository's work grows from and lands on.
Accepting a session's work: merged into the line, or put on a branch of its own.
The move that takes what was offered: a session's work in its review, which lands it, or a proposal.
terms.why: 采纳 is taking what was proposed; 接受 is the declaration's accepts.

terms.means: A branch rule's switch: a quest's done lands its work as the person's accept would, and the rule's plugin pushes it and opens the pull request with no press.
terms.why: Approve is the go-ahead's press (放行), a different yes, so auto-approve would give one act two names (D145).

terms.means: Read what a session changed before accepting it, sending it back or discarding it.
terms.why: 改动 is the diff's changes, and 查看 any look.

terms.means: Where a repository's work runs for the person to look at before it lands: local, shown in Daoris's browser at the address where the app normally runs, or deployed, such as dev, reached by the repository's documented route; never production (D154).
terms.why: 审阅 is review's own word, so the place a review happens takes it; 预览 is a preview of a file, and 审查 an inspection someone else performs.

terms.means: A chain's quest that shows the chain's work in a review environment for the person's look, then waits for their verdict (D154 point 4).
terms.why: 搭建 is putting something up to be looked at; 设置 is a setting's word and 部署 a deploy's, which a local set-up is not.

terms.means: One showing a set-up step said: where to look, what it shows, how to show it again, and the commit Daoris read; what a verdict answers (D154 point 9).
terms.why: The step's own word, so the showing and its step say one thing.

terms.means: The person's verdict that a set-up showed the work right, which lets the work it holds land (D154 point 8).
terms.why: The verdict is the review done, so 已 and review's own word.

terms.means: The person's verdict that a set-up is not right yet, with their words, which go to the set-up step's session as its next turn (D154 point 8).
terms.why: What a person says looking at work that is not right: it is neither a denial (拒绝) nor a decline (谢绝), and the work goes on.

terms.means: The person lets a chain's work in a repository land without being shown to them, with their words where they give any (D154 point 3, the table's first row).
terms.why: 跳过 is passing over a step; 忽略 would say it was never seen.

terms.means: Serve a set-up's build to its tab of Daoris's browser again and bring the tab forward, with no session and no model (D154 point 8).
terms.why: 展示 is the set-up's own act, shown to the person; a reload (刷新) is another act, which loads the person's own server once Daoris no longer serves the tab, and a sentence saying so names it rightly.

terms.means: One agent's reading of another session's work before it lands: what it read, its findings and its limits, bound to the commits it read (D155 point 1).
terms.why: 意见 is a view someone gives, as this is; review's word 审阅 stays the person's (D154 point 8), and 审查 or 评审 would be an inspection that settles something.

terms.means: The agent that gives a second opinion, from another maker where one can (D155 point 4).
terms.why: 阅读 is what it does; 审阅者 would give it the person's word for a review, which no agent gives.

terms.means: One claim in a second opinion, with where it is and why it matters: a claim, never a fact (D155 point 8); and a place where two repositories reached one conclusion (convergence).
terms.why: 发现 is something found, as both are; 问题 would call a claim a defect before any check established one.

terms.means: A must finding the working session did not fix and no recheck withdrew, which waits for the person's answer (D155 point 8).
terms.why: 争议 is two sides disagreeing, which a dispute is; 冲突 is a merge's word.

terms.means: Return a session's work to it with a note, so it carries on.
Throw away a session's tree and the work in it.
Give a landed branch to a plugin, which pushes it and opens the pull request.
After a pull request merges: fetch each repository, move its line forward and clean up the branches that landed.
terms.why: 同步 is sync's word; 更新 is the plain word for bringing something current.

terms.means: Remove what a session left once its work is on the line: its tree and its branch.
Git's merge: one of a landing's two forms, into the line.
Send commits to a git remote; Daoris never does it on its own.
A git commit.
Git's fetch: read a remote's branches without moving anything here.
A code host's request to merge a branch, which a plugin may open.
terms.why: The code host's own Chinese name for it.

terms.means: A repository's own git remote, such as origin; not the workspace's remote.
A shared Daoris deployment a workspace is wired to, where its quests and records sync.
terms.why: Kept apart from a git remote (远程仓库).

terms.means: Connect a workspace to a remote, with the deployment's address and a key.
A running Daoris service, which a remote points at.
Exchange a workspace's quests and records with its remote.
Daoris's knowledge service, which holds the quests, the asks and the index.
What the service has read of every repository's knowledge.
How search answers, by words or by meaning too; the tier that answered is said on every screen.
Where two repositories learned the same thing in different words, found by the index.
terms.why: 殊途同归: different roads, one destination.

terms.means: Finding knowledge across the family by words, or by meaning where a model is set.
A workspace drawn: its repositories, the quests between them and what they learned in common.
A repository's modules drawn in layers, from the map it keeps.
What the map draws between two repositories: quests, asks, a chain, a dependency, or the same thing learned.
terms.why: *Lines* was also Settings' lines (主线).

terms.means: What a repository has written down for others: its rules, knowledge documents, skills and decisions.
One document the index holds.
The rules, knowledge and skills a repository follows, from the canon and its own.
terms.why: 教义 is a religion's word.

terms.means: The shared doctrine Daoris ships and syncs into every adopting repository; canonical material came from it.
A repository's own material, never synced; and what stays on this machine.
An always-loaded piece of doctrine; and a line of the rules saying what an agent may do.
A procedure an agent invokes by name.
A named set of rules, knowledge and skills a repository opts into.
terms.why: 包 alone is any package.

terms.means: A repository takes on Daoris's doctrine, with a manifest and a lock of its own.
terms.why: 加入, 采用 and 接入 were three words for it, and 接入 reads as connecting.

terms.means: A synced file edited in the repository, so it no longer matches its lock.
The coding agent a session runs on, named by its product: Claude Code, Codex and the rest.
terms.why: 工具 is also a tool call's word, and 代理 a proxy's.

terms.means: The code's word for an agent; never on the window.
An agent a session starts to work beside it.
One call an agent made: a read, an edit, a command.
Who an agent signs in as: a sign-in or an API key.
The code's word for an account; never on the window.
How Daoris talks to an agent: directly (直连), or over the protocol (协议).
The language model an account's agent runs, or search uses.
How hard an agent's model reasons, where it offers a choice.
What a session's model holds at once, as the agent reports it.
What each account has carried, measured and never priced.
Let an agent's account in: the tool's own sign-in, a page and a code.
terms.why: *Log in* was a second English word for the same act.

terms.means: An account that is a key rather than a sign-in.
Make Daoris run one version of an agent, installed where Daoris keeps it.
A release of an agent, a plugin or a tool.
A program Daoris runs beside its agents: Git, Node.js, PowerShell, GitHub CLI, Azure CLI.
terms.why: The agent term keeps 工具 out of a label naming an agent, and a tool call keeps its own 工具调用; so *Tools* names one thing (D121 §4.4).

terms.means: A tool's version Daoris downloads into its home, verifies and runs; for an agent the word is *pin*.
terms.why: One of three ways offered side by side, and the owner's own word (*self managed*); a pin is one press on an agent's row from its maker's channel.

terms.means: The address of a list of tools' versions and where each downloads, read before the one built in.
terms.why: Named for what it is, the place a resource list is read from; a location is never fetched until the person looks.

terms.means: Put an agent, or one of Daoris's own plugins, on this machine.
Replace an agent or a plugin with its newer release.
A folder that declares agents and servers and may speak at points; never code loaded into Daoris.
Switch a plugin on, so the driver asks it at its points and hands sessions what it declares; its state is on (已启用).
terms.why: 开启 paired with 关闭, close's name, so the switch read as open and close. 启用 and 停用 say what the switch does to the plugin and nothing else (NAME2).

terms.means: Switch a plugin off: it stays installed, and the driver asks it nothing and hands sessions nothing it declares; its state is off (已停用).
terms.why: 关闭 is close's name, so the press read as close and an off plugin wore a closed quest's 已关闭; 禁用 says forbidden, where the person only set it aside (NAME2).

terms.means: Where a plugin speaks: before a start, after a session ends, once a landing has made its branch.
A program a plugin hands every session to talk to, over MCP.
Start a plugin as the driver would, send it a sample at each point, and read every answer with the driver's reader.
terms.why: 测试 is a plugins repository's own tests, which a trial is not. *Try again* is a retry (重试), not a trial, so it is not this term.

terms.means: End an account's cool-off early, so the next start may run on it: the person may know its limit was raised, and if it still holds the agent refuses at once and the account cools again (D125 §2.3).
terms.why: Neither a plugin's trial (试运行) nor a quest's retry (重试): it offers an account again, so it takes words of its own (TOOL4g).

terms.means: A plugin's own tests, which `node --test` runs in its folder; a trial is not one.
terms.why: A term so a sentence that names a plugin's tests and its trial together says 测试 for the tests without reading as a trial called 测试.

terms.means: The plugins the install carries, installed only by a press; `offer` is its code word, never a label.
terms.why: The install carries them, so 自带; the avoid list is empty, since `--offer` is a flag people type.

terms.means: A plugin's answer at quest/consider that keeps a quest from starting, until it answers otherwise.
terms.why: A plugin's decision is not the person's hold of a repository (暂停), so it takes a word of its own in each language.

terms.means: What a plugin keeps: an update never touches it, and a removal leaves it.
The part of Daoris that starts and watches sessions on this machine.
terms.why: 驱动器 is a disk drive.

terms.means: The driver's rounds of looking at what to start, every few seconds while Daoris runs; one round is its look (一轮).
The code's word for one round of the driver loop; the window says the driver's next look, 一轮.
The person stops the driver starting sessions in a repository, until they resume it (恢复).
A session stops at a checkpoint for its person, or a quest stops after too many failed sessions, until the person answers.
terms.why: 暂停 is hold's word, and 搁置 a quest sitting.

terms.means: Stop an ask's or a quest's work on this machine for now: what of it runs is stopped, nothing of it starts, and everything stays as it was until you resume it (恢复).
terms.why: A hold stops nothing that runs and a pause does, so they are two names; 暂停 is hold's, 挂起 park's, 搁置 sitting's and 中止 an end, and 暂缓 is what a team says of an ask set aside for now (D132 §8.2).

terms.means: Give up an ask's or a quest's work on this machine for good: its quests declined with your reason, what only Daoris holds of it discarded, its sessions archived; what reached any other branch is kept.
terms.why: Clean up (清理) removes what landed and keeps exactly what this throws away, so a destructive press must not wear a safe press's name; discard (丢弃) is one tree's. The English words the design avoids, clean up and cancel, are other things' names, so only the Chinese list holds them (D132 §8.2).

terms.means: A quest open and not started, with the driver's reason.
A session that ended in failure, counted against its quest until the quest parks.
The code's word for a failed session counted against its quest; never on the window.
What waits for the person: a parked session, a proposal, an ask its intake asked about; everything What needs you lists.
An agent's own permission to work in a folder, which the person grants.
What an agent may do: the allow, ask and deny lists handed to every session.
A change an agent or Ask Daoris proposes; nothing applies until the person accepts or applies it.
Make an Ask Daoris proposal real, through the same door its screen uses.
A conversation about Daoris itself, which reads, explains and proposes.
terms.why: 问道 is to ask after the Way, and 道衍 is Daoris's own name.

terms.means: One question to Ask Daoris from the palette, without opening the side bar.
The product, said so in running text; 道衍 is its wordmark, its menu, and Ask Daoris's name (问道衍).
The computer this window runs on.
What happens on this machine, a line an event, without anyone's words.
The folder that holds everything Daoris keeps on this machine.
The region at the window's right, holding Ask Daoris and the attended session's views.
The region under the centre, holding the console and the terminal.
Sessions' own list at its left, grouped by what each session needs from you (by state), or by repository.
Start a quest's work again on this machine: one parked after its failed sessions, or one your stop holds.
terms.why: `retry` is the command's word, which sentences name in backticks, so no English word is avoided (SESSUX1d, D126 §8).

terms.means: A quest's few words, written by whoever publishes it, shown where a list gives it one line; where none was given, the service names the quest from its own words.
terms.why: 简称 is an abbreviation and 副标题 a subtitle; the words are the publisher's own (SESSUX1j, D126 §8).

terms.means: Take an ended session out of the session list on this machine, kept whole; its inverse, unarchive (取消归档), brings it back.
terms.why: 存档 is a game's save, and 隐藏 promises less than archive keeps (SESSUX1e, D126 §8).

terms.means: The raw view of what a session printed.
A shell of the person's own, in the panel.
What was observed of a session: its process, its quest's moves, what landed.
A file from a session's tree, or its landed branch, read in the side bar.
A window with a tile per running session.
The command palette: every view and act, by name, from the keyboard.
What is set: a repository's or a workspace's, on its page's Setup tab, and a machine's, the steps Get started walks.
terms.why: Setup names the tab since UX6j (D150 §2.3); the guide that walks a machine's setup is Get started.

terms.means: Settings' first domain: the steps a machine needs before Daoris can drive, each with its doors and its commands.
terms.why: Its name in D97, again since UX6j (D150 §2.3), because Setup names a repository's and a workspace's tab and one word names one thing.

terms.means: The jobs Daoris gives a model or an agent of its own: search and convergence, Ask Daoris, intake.
terms.why: *Daoris's own AI* was a possessive, and 「Daoris 自身的 AI」 the possessive translated.

terms.means: The browser Daoris starts, its own or your Edge, where sessions and you sign in to sites.
A page Daoris keeps for you, in a folder on its browser's bookmarks bar.
The session shown in Sessions' centre.
A session gives its quest back, since another holds its repository.
What a session does with the person's words after its turn, its park or its end: the same session goes on in its own conversation (MSG1, D137).
terms.why: Resume stays the code's word and the press that undoes a pause or a hold (恢复, D132); on the window a conversation goes on (继续) or is continued (接续), never resumed (D137 §5.1).

terms.means: The application's own page of domains, and what is true about this machine.

accepted._why: Budget judgements looked at and kept (NAME2; docs/2026-10-01-naming-design.md §6): the length is the name, and the element it renders in gives it more room than its kind's budget assumes, or a placeholder's typical value overstates it. Each holds the name it accepted in each language it accepts, and why, naming the room the code gives the element; the window confirms the room. scripts/names-check.mjs stops reporting a name while it is the one accepted, and reports it again once it is renamed, or once it fits and the acceptance can go.

names.why: A press in the second opinion's gate, on a wrapping row of its own beside at most three others in a main area at least 400px wide (XAGENT1g); the design names it whole (D155 §8.4–§8.5), since what it asks is the working agent's own in a fresh conversation, which is never an independent reading.

A run step's state on its pill, on a wrapping line of its own beside at most *this session* and a time, in a side bar at least 300px wide (WORKFLOW1c); the design names the state whole (D157 §5.2), and a shorter word would not say whom the work waits on.

names.en: Skip the review for this work…
names.why: A press in a review's gate, on a wrapping row of its own beside at most three others in a main area at least 400px wide (REVIEWENV1g); the design names it whole (D154 §3.6), since what is skipped is this work's review and no other's.

A press in a review's gate, on a wrapping row of its own in a main area at least 400px wide (REVIEWENV1g); the environment is the person's own name for it, which `dev` or `local` is, so the typical value's ten overstates it.

names.zh: 打开智能体可以做什么
names.why: A door under its setup step's text, which drops under the text when there is no room beside it (SETUP1a), so the button is as wide as its words; it names the section of the agent's page it opens (UX6e), where *Open Agents* would not say which part.
Beside an account's state on its row, which wraps (UX6e); the placeholder is a clock, *10:42*, five units where the typical value counts ten.
An item in an account's ⋯, a menu at least 13rem wide and as wide as its longest item (UX6e); the workspace is the person's own name for it.
An item in an account's ⋯, beside *Use by default*, in the same menu as wide as its longest item (UX6e); the workspace is the person's own name for it.
An item in an account's ⋯, a menu as wide as its longest item (UX7b, D152 §4.2); the workspace is the person's own name for it, and the list is what it joins.
An item in an account's ⋯, a menu as wide as its longest item (UX7b); *this machine's list* is the one list no workspace names, and a shorter word would not say which.
An item in an account's ⋯, a menu as wide as its longest item (UX7b, D152 §4.2); it takes the account out of that list alone, which the name says.
An item in an account's ⋯, a menu as wide as its longest item (UX7b); it takes the account out of the one list no workspace names.
Add an account's first step names the account its sign-in reaches (UX7b, D152 §4.5), the press that would have stopped ACCT1; the account is the person's name for it.
In an account's *Runs for* column, which wraps (UX7b, D152 §4.2); the scope is a workspace's own name, and the mark says its starts begin there.

Beside *cooling* in an account's state column, which wraps (UX7b, D152 §4.2); the time is the hold's end, the reset its agent named or Daoris's default (D125 §2.4), said whole so the person knows when it is offered again; a reported reset is said beside its window instead (ACCTUX1).
A row's *Use in a workspace…* panel's name for a reader, never drawn as a heading (UX7b); the account is the person's own name for it.

A select's option, not a segmented one: the trigger is as wide as its row's control column and its list as wide as it needs, and the name is the driver's table's (Simplified Chinese (简体中文)), so the choice says which language it takes, not only that it inherits (LANG1c).

names.en: dev writes allowed; test locally against dev; prod only on a yes
names.zh: 允许写入开发环境；在本地对开发环境测试；生产环境须经你同意
names.why: The example in a standing answer's three-row box on a repository's page, which wraps; it is the answer the evidence shows a person gave once and no later session read (KNOWUSE1b), so the example is the whole sentence.

The one control of a Setup row whose value stands from above, alone in its row's control column, which keeps half the row at the main area's width and stacks under the label below 26rem; it says whose the value becomes, which the redesign names it for (UX6f, D150 §4.2).
A workspace's Setup row's control, in the same column as a repository's *Set for this repository* (UX6g, D150 §4.3): it says whose the default becomes, the workspace's rather than Daoris's.

A door under its setup step's text, which drops under the text when there is no room beside it (SETUP1a), so the button is as wide as its words; it names the page it opens, the workspace's Setup (UX6g), where *Open Workspace* named a Settings domain that is gone.

A segmented option in a scope on an agent's page (Settings → Agents' until UX6e), a row whose control takes its own line below 26rem; the design names it so (D130 §16.6), and a shorter one lost what it promises.
The other segmented option beside it, in the same row; the design names it so (D130 §16.6), and both halves of it are the setting.

A segmented option under a workspace on an agent's page (Settings → Agents' until UX6e), a row whose control takes its own line below 26rem; the design names it so (D130 §9), and *this machine* is the glossary's name.
A pill on an account's row in a scope's list, a row that wraps; the setting's own name lower-cased, which the design keeps (D130 §9).
The move in a confirming pair under a workspace's scope, on a line of its own with the sentence it confirms; it names the choice it makes.
A pill beside the sitting reason on a quest's page, whose fact column wraps; the design names it so (D125 §4).
The preview tab's tip and accessible name: the tab shows the file's name, cut with the path in this tip (TABS1).

names.zh: 正在操作 Daoris 浏览器的会话
names.why: The group label of the browser door's menu, which is 18rem wide (w-72), past the 260px a card's section is measured by.

names.en: Links — a ticket, a page, a document; one per line
names.zh: 链接——工单、页面、文档；每行一个
names.why: A form's label above its box, where it wraps; the qualifier after the dash is the field's instruction (NAME1a's audit kept it).

names.en: Nobody yet — let the declarations propose
names.zh: 暂不指定——由声明来提议
names.why: A select's option in the ask composer: the field grows to it, so its room is the field's, not a segment's 90px.
A select's option in the start form carrying the account's name; its room is the field's. *Signed out* is the state's one word on the Agents place too (UX6e, D150 §5.3).
A select's option for an account's model and effort; its room is the field's, and own says the agent chooses, not Daoris.

names.en: An act, once a landing has made its branch
names.zh: 一个动作，在落地已建好它的分支之后
names.why: A point's gloss: a checkbox's label after the point's name in the kit, which wraps, and the point's line on a plugin's page; it says when the point speaks (NAME1a's audit kept it).

names.en: A decision, before a planned start spends anything
names.zh: 一个决定，在计划的启动花费任何东西之前
names.why: A point's gloss: a checkbox's label after the point's name in the kit, which wraps, and the point's line on a plugin's page; it says when the point speaks (NAME1a's audit kept it).

names.en: An observation, after a session ends
names.zh: 一次观察，在会话结束之后
names.why: A point's gloss: a checkbox's label after the point's name in the kit, which wraps, and the point's line on a plugin's page; it says when the point speaks (NAME1a's audit kept it).
A select's option; its room is the field's, and the qualifier after the dash says what still answers with no agent.
A select's option; its room is the field's, and the qualifier after the dash says what still answers with no agent.

The term's own name in a segment; Daoris is six Latin letters at half a unit each, so it reads within the segment's 90px.
A select's option carrying the plugin's id; its room is the field's.
A select's option in the start form; its room is the field's.
A select's option naming what a start runs on where the machine has a default (UX5 U67); its room is the field's.
The confirming press in the ask page's close form, a row in the main area that wraps; not the side bar's two-button room.
A proposal row's press on the ask page, naming the repository it publishes to; the main area, not the side bar.
An icon control's tip and accessible name on the strip; nothing lays the words out.
The code map's page action in the main area's header, beside the title; not the side bar.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the list pane's close; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the list strip's open; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
A press in Settings' agent card, on a row that wraps beside Add API key; a shorter name lost another (NAME1a's audit kept it).
A ghost press on its own line in the map's detail panel, not one of two side by side.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the list pane's close; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the list strip's open; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
The confirming press in the quest page's decline form, a row in the main area that wraps.
The accessible name of the × beside a repository's chip in Settings; it names both repositories, and nothing lays it out.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the list pane's close; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the list strip's open; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
A press in Settings' Updates card; with a count of one digit it is 20 characters, where the check measures a count as two.
The term's own name and its count, the second press under Updates (NAME1b); with a count of one digit it is 20 characters.
The one primary control in Setup's head, not the side bar (NAME1a's audit kept it).
The confirming press alone on its row: in the parked band's form under the session's head, and as the answer composer's send, which has no endings or attachments beside it.

names.en: write to it — the same session goes on with your words
names.zh: 写给它——同一个会话会带着你的话继续
names.why: The hint in the box at the foot of a session's page, which is the centre's width, never narrower than its 400px floor; the design names it so (D137 §5.1), and what the words will do is the whole of it.

names.en: Start a conversation with these words
names.why: The one press under the line saying the words cannot go on, alone on its row in the conversation's column at the centre's width; the design names it so (D137 §5.1), since a new conversation, not this one, is what it starts.

names.en: Go on in a new session
names.why: The one press under words a cooling account holds, alone on its row in the conversation's column at the centre's width; the design names it so (D137 §5.1), since a new session, not this one, is what goes on (MSG1g2).
The confirming press in the parked band's form under the session's head, a row that wraps.
An icon control's tip and accessible name in the side bar's head; nothing lays the words out.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the session list's close; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
An icon control's tip and accessible name, the session list strip's open; nothing lays the words out, and every view's list names its pair alike.
A link on its own line in the review's footer and in a landed branch's note: the side bar's whole width, not half of it.
A chip on an agent's way in, in Settings' agent card, naming the plugin it came from, which is the point (NAME1a's audit kept it).
An account's name in Settings' row when the agent does not say who, and a meta word beside a name that repeats; no pill holds it.
Words in the pin's row in Settings' agent card, not a pill; PATH is four Latin letters at half a unit each.
A pill in the pin's row in Settings' agent card, a row that wraps; the version is the point, and a version is about six characters.
A pill in the pin's row in Settings' agent card, a row that wraps; the version is the point, and a version is about six characters.
A chip in the Manage drawer, not a pill beside a row's title; git is three Latin letters at half a unit each.
The pill in a tool's card header in Settings, carrying the version, which is about six characters.

A dot's word on a What needs you row, in Overview's main area, in a row that wraps; no pill holds it.

names.why: A dot's word on a What needs you row, in Overview's main area, in a row that wraps; no pill holds it.

A press on a What needs you row naming the repositories it publishes to, in Overview's main area on a row that wraps, not the side bar (UX6c, D150 §6.2).
A press on a What needs you row, in Overview's main area on a row that wraps; the design names it so (D150 §6.2), and it says the choice it opens.
A dot's word on a What needs you row, in Overview's main area, in a row that wraps; no pill holds it, and it is the quest page's word for the same wait (UX6d, D125 §4).
A press on a What needs you row naming the account it lets in and the workspace that waits, in Overview's main area on a row that wraps; the account-use design names it so (D130 §9, UX6d).

names.en: waiting for the conversation to open
names.why: The line above the composer's box saying what waits for the turn, at the centre's width; no pill holds it.

names.en: waiting for this turn to end
names.why: The line above the composer's box saying what waits for the turn, at the centre's width; no pill holds it.
A panel tab's tip and accessible name, its kind and state; the tab shows its name and a mark.
The status item's tip and accessible name; the bar shows its icon and its count.
Its counts are single digits, of five or six steps, so 配置：2/6 is 4.5 units; the check measures each count as two.
A dot's word at the end of a tool call's row in the conversation, at the centre's width; no pill holds it.

names.why: An item of the side bar's views menu, which grows to 20rem; the view's name fills the placeholder, and right side bar is the region's name in every label beside it.
